Subject: Finova — Performance SLO & multi-region routing (recap + next steps)

Hi Roberta — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key requirements we heard
- Latency SLOs: 95th p95 token latency targets by region: US <= 250ms, EU <= 300ms, APAC <= 400ms (first-token and steady-state streaming expectations differ; see notes)
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline ~200 RPS sustained, expected concurrency ~500 active sessions, peak burst up to ~1.5k RPS for short windows (5–15m)
- Response size: median ~120 tokens, 95th ~450 tokens (important for throughput calculus)
- Streaming: server-sent events / chunked streaming required for conversational UX — first-byte goal ~150–200ms for streaming endpoints
- Data residency: EU-customer traffic and logs MUST remain in EU; APAC data routing preferred for APAC customers. Finova cannot replicate EU PII outside EU region without prior approval.
- SLO enforcement & fallbacks: need automatic regional routing with fallback to another region only if allowed by residency policy; ability to degrade to smaller models for cost/availability fallbacks but with configurable quality thresholds

What Redwood can do (high-level)
- Regional model replicas: we can spin up model replicas in US/EU/APAC with routing policies (geo by user IP / account mapping) and per-region capacity reservations (Dedicated nodes)
- Streaming support: low-latency streaming (SSE/chunked) is supported; can tune batching to prioritize first-token latency when needed
- Data residency: for strict EU residency we recommend either Dedicated in-region capacity or Private deployment (VPC) with EU-only storage paths and KMS in-region
- Autoscaling & burst capacity: we can provide burst pools and capacity reservations to handle 1.5k RPS peaks; need final traffic patterns to size correctly

Open questions / items for Finova
1) Can you share a 30-day traffic distribution (by minute-level if possible) and a sample session profile (tokens per response)? I attached a short SLO template to capture these numbers.
2) For EU data, do you require zero-cross-region replication for logs/metrics as well (analytics vs audit logs distinction)?
3) Which endpoints must be streaming vs batch? (chat, summarization, reranking, embeddings)

Next steps
- Marissa (me) to send this recap + SLO spreadsheet (attached) — done
- Technical deep-dive with Aditya + Dev to size model replicas and confirm streaming tuning — propose Wed 02/12 or Thu 02/13 (30–60m)
- Preliminary capacity & pricing estimate shared within 3 business days after deep-dive

Thanks — we’ll come prepared with a proposed deployment topology (regional replicas + routing policy) and baseline numbers for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: Finova_SLO_requirements_v1.xlsx (XLSX), regional-routing-diagram.png (PNG)

Best,

Thanks Marissa — the recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming: yes — SSE is preferred for the UI. For initial token we’d like as close to ~100–200ms as possible on US/EU traffic; APAC we accept ~200–350ms given network constraints. 
- Throughput: the 1.5k bursts are real (marketing sends can spike traffic). We can provide a 7-day sample of minute-level traffic by EOD today.
- Data residency: EU "must not leave EU" applies to both request payloads and audit logs containing PII. Analytics aggregates (non-PII) can be replicated outside EU.

Also: are there any limitations on streaming with quantized model variants? We plan to use a 4-bit quantized model if it impacts latency/throughput tradeoffs.

We’re good to do Thu 02/13 for the technical deep-dive — can you do 10:00am PT?

Appreciate it,

Subject: Re: Finova — Performance SLO & multi-region routing (recap + next steps)

Roberta — quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow’s deep-dive. Short answers: 

- Streaming + quantization: Supported. 4-bit quantized models are compatible with streaming but you’ll see some tradeoffs: quantization reduces memory and improves throughput per-GPU, but depending on kernel availability it can slightly increase first-token latency versus full-fp16 paths. We can mitigate with CPU pre-warm, smaller initial-batch config, and KV cache priming.

- First-token latency: to hit ~100–200ms first-byte we recommend the following per-region config:
  * Dedicated regional replicas (US/EU) for low-latency paths
  * Small initial-batch window (variable 1–4ms) and prefer async I/O path for streaming
  * Reserve a small pool of warm workers for hot endpoints (pre-warmed model instances)

- Throughput & concurrency sizing (initial proposal):
  * Sustained: 200 RPS => ~2 dedicated vGPU shards (model/architecture dependent) per region for 120-token median responses
  * Concurrency target 500 active sessions => 4–6 shards per region to keep p95 latency targets under budget (estimate needs validation with sample traffic)
  * Burst capacity to 1.5k RPS => enable burst pool with autoscale and short-lived spot-backed workers; will need commit / reserve to guarantee SLAs during high-volume marketing events

- Regional routing & residency: We support account-level routing (map customers to a region) + geo-IP routing. For strict EU-only residency we recommend either Dedicated EU capacity or Private (VPC) with EU storage/KMS. Audit logs with PII should be stored in-region — we can export encrypted logs to your EU KMS.

- Next steps: please share the 7-day minute-level traffic dump and a couple of sample sessions (JSON traces). We’ll run a quick synthetic to validate the shard counts and bring a recommended capacity diagram tomorrow.

I’ll be on the call Thu 02/13 10:00am PT — joining with Dev who will cover autoscaling/burst.

Thanks,
